title: Servers
noContainers: No containers running (they appear a few seconds after the agent reports).
containerRemoveBody: This force-removes the container "{name}" on this server. Managed Tugra apps/databases are deleted from their own page — this is only for foreign containers. Type the name to confirm:
activityDesc: Every action taken on this server — who did what, newest first.
proxyDesc: The reverse proxy that routes traffic and manages SSL for apps with a domain.
empty: Connect your first server to start deploying apps and databases.
name: Server name (e.g. web-1)
installDesc: Run this command on your server (token embedded):
waiting: Waiting for the agent to connect…
bulkNamesHint: {n} server(s) will be created — each gets its own install command.
bulkCreatedHint: Run each command on its server (or copy all and run them in turn). Each server shows PENDING until its agent connects.
noCloudCredential: No Hetzner provider is set up for this team.
deleteServerDesc: Remove this server from Tugra. Its apps and metrics are dropped from the panel.
destroyVmHint: Tugra created this VM — leave this checked to delete it at the provider and stop billing. Uncheck to keep the VM running.
troubleshootHint: Make sure you ran the command on the server, that it can reach this hub over the network (outbound WebSocket), and check the agent logs. The enroll token is valid for one hour — get a fresh command if it has expired.
noMetrics: No metrics yet — live stream starts when the agent connects.
capabilitiesDesc: What the hub is allowed to do on this server. Turn off anything you don't need — the terminal (interactive shell) is off by default on new servers.
cleanupDesc: Removes unused images, containers, networks and build cache.
cleanupCronHint: A cron expression (minute hour day month weekday) runs cleanup at a fixed time and overrides the hourly interval. Example: 0 3 * * * runs at 03:00 daily.
discoverDesc: Scan this server for containers not yet managed by Tugra and adopt them as apps.
noForeignContainers: No unmanaged containers found on this server.
adoptDataWarning: Adopting only renames the container. A later redeploy from Tugra recreates it and will NOT carry over its volumes or bind-mounted data — set up matching volumes first if you need the data.
adoptImageWarning: Tugra will pull this image on the next redeploy, so make sure the server can reach it (locally-built images that were never pushed will fail).
networkDesc: Set a wildcard domain to serve apps at *.your-domain, override the magic suffix, or pin a public IP. Changes regenerate this server's magic domains (apply on next deploy).
dnsProviderHint: lego provider name — e.g. cloudflare, route53, digitalocean.
dnsCredsHint: One KEY=VALUE per line (e.g. CF_DNS_API_TOKEN=…). Stored encrypted; use a least-privilege, zone-scoped token. Leave blank to keep the current credentials.
tunnelDesc: Expose this server's apps to the internet with no public IP and no port-forwarding — Tugra runs cloudflared and routes traffic through Cloudflare. Enable it per app from each app's Expose settings.
tunnelCertWarn: This server's certificate mode isn't Plain HTTP. Cloudflare terminates TLS at its edge for tunnel traffic, so set HTTPS certificates to Plain HTTP to avoid a redirect loop while the tunnel is active.
tunnelApiTokenHint: Create a token with Zone:DNS Edit, Zone:Zone Read and Account:Cloudflare Tunnel Edit. Stored encrypted; never a Global API Key.
tunnelWildcardHint: Where apps are served, e.g. apps.example.com. Defaults to the zone. A wildcard CNAME is created for it.
tunnelDisconnectConfirm: Disconnect the Cloudflare Tunnel? This stops cloudflared, deletes the tunnel and its wildcard DNS record. Apps will no longer be reachable through it.
tunnelNotConfigured: No Cloudflare Tunnel is configured for this server.
tunnelSetupFailed: Couldn't connect the tunnel. Check the API token, account ID and zone.
